sections.title: In one minute
items: Azure DevOps is a platform of integrated services for software teams. You connect to an organization, which holds projects. Each project can use all five services, and they link to each other: a pull request links to a work item, a pipeline run links to the commit, a test links to the build.

cards.text: Git and TFVC, pull requests, branch policies. [Open](#repos)

cards.title: Pipelines
cards.text: CI/CD in YAML or classic, on hosted or your own agents. [Open](#pipelines)

items: Two hosting options exist: Azure DevOps Services (cloud) and Azure DevOps Server (on premises). This topic describes Services and notes Server where a page does.

sections.title: Typical flow

items: Plan: create work items in Boards and put them in a sprint
Code: branch in Repos and open a pull request that links the work item
Build: a pipeline triggers on the push, builds and publishes artifacts
Test: automated tests run in the pipeline; Test Plans covers manual tests
Package: libraries go to an Artifacts feed
Deploy: a deployment job targets an environment with approvals and checks
The pipeline part is the one with a language of its own: see the [YAML tab](#yaml-index).

sections.title: Hosting, agents and cost
items: Jobs run on agents. Microsoft-hosted agents are fresh VMs per job; self-hosted agents run on your machines. See [Agents](#agents).

The free tier includes the first five users (Basic), one Microsoft-hosted CI/CD job (up to 30 hours a month), one self-hosted job, unlimited private Git repositories and 2 GiB of Artifacts storage. Charges appear on an Azure subscription bill.

items.text: Paid access (Basic + Test Plans, more parallel jobs, more Artifacts storage) is not covered here beyond a mention. See [Organization](#organization).

sections.title: What it is
items: Azure Boards is the work tracking service. A work item is the unit: a user story, bug, task, feature or epic. Everything else shows work items in a different way.

items: A deployment job is a special job for deploying to an environment. It records deployment history on the environment and downloads the available artifacts automatically. It uses a strategy: runOnce, rolling or canary.

sections.title: Steps
items: A step is the smallest unit. The first key names the type: script, bash, pwsh, powershell, checkout, download, downloadBuild, getPackage, publish, reviewApp, task or template. That key is required and comes first.
All of them except task and template are shortcuts for a task. Every step accepts condition, continueOnError, displayName, target, enabled, env, name, timeoutInMinutes and retryCountOnTaskFailure.
